A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowCast study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SEVIR and ARSO forecasting experiments, baseline comparisons, CFM-versus-diffusion ablations, sampling-efficiency results and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline, spatial-skill, extreme-event and solver-comparison results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 changes the reported backbone width from 196 to 192 and time-embedding dimension from 784 to 768. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects retraining or a documentation correction. The VAE, I-CFM objective and Euler inference remain unchanged; Algorithms 1–2 make existing procedures explicit.

E1.justification: Both versions use SEVIR and ARSO radar nowcasting with 13 input frames and 12 forecast frames at five-minute intervals. Added extreme-threshold results and ARSO lead-time curves analyze the retained datasets and task, without introducing new populations or environments.

E2.justification: Earthfarseer, previously only discussed in related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 3–4 and the qualitative comparisons, including Appendix A.2. Its CSI-M is 0.389 on SEVIR and 0.368 on ARSO. The other baseline methods and the diffusion-objective comparator are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds FSS over 16-by-16 neighborhoods and expands threshold-specific evaluation to CSI, HSS and FAR over the forecast sequence. It corrects the ARSO training count from 63,716 to 38,229 in the prose, matching the unchanged Table 1, and revises the reported model dimensions. These changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 extends extreme-event analysis with threshold-specific detection and false-alarm results in Table 5 and supplies numerical evidence for the already-described solver study in Table 9. One-step sampling was already examined in v1 Figure 5. The objective-ablation table loses its final-frame CSI results. These extend and revise existing analytical questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Eight-member forecast ensembles and the Gaussian approximation used for CRPS are retained; additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared scores in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged, but v3 adds Earthfarseer and FSS results, extreme-event scores, ARSO lead-time curves and solver accuracy/runtime results. For example, FlowCast's newly reported FSS is 0.767 on SEVIR and 0.738 on ARSO. Table 6 adds explicit one-step results while removing v1 Table 5's final-frame CSI columns. This substantially expands reported evidence without demonstrating a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1.3 introduces mathematical definitions of neighborhood exceedance fractions and the newly adopted FSS metric in Equation 5. The CFM probability path, target field, loss and existing metric equations are retained. No theorem, proof or formal guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion narrow the broad first-application claim to a fully probabilistic, direct noise-to-data CFM framework, distinguished from forecast-refinement approaches. The central claims of strong performance on SEVIR and ARSO and superior accuracy-efficiency relative to the matched diffusion model remain.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands the proposed mechanism: straight transport trajectories are argued to provide a favorable temporal-coherence prior, and nonzero path variance is described as stabilizing regularization. It also adds explanations of training stability, dataset-dependent VAE convergence and detection/false-alarm tradeoffs. The radar-only and two-dataset limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 documents ARSO replication padding to 304-by-416 and subsequent cropping, CRPS normalization by 255 or 57, and adaptive-solver tolerances of 10^-2 and 10^-3. It also supplies an explicit code-repository URL. These supplement the extensive existing implementation details; the PDFs do not establish new preprocessing or independently verify repository availability.

R1.justification: V3 replaces the claim that CFM scientific forecasting is unexplored with a substantive comparison to Feng et al. (2025), characterized as deterministic forecast refinement. FlowCast is repositioned around standalone probabilistic generation. Chen et al. (2018) and Liu et al. (2023) support an expanded CNF/rectified-flow discussion, while the Dao and Jin citations are removed.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites revise the opening motivation, flow-related discussion and performance interpretation. Related work gains numbered subsections, training/sampling lists become pseudocode, and results distinguish general from extreme-event performance. The main section sequence and much of the methodological and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the training/sampling schematic with two algorithm boxes, adds an ARSO lead-time figure and extreme-event and solver tables, and expands benchmark-table structures. Qualitative figures throughout the paper and appendix gain Earthfarseer rows and vertical color bars. The architecture and sampling-efficiency graphics are retained, with substantial redistribution of displays.

improvement.justification: V3 better supports the existing conclusions through spatial and extreme-event evaluation and numerical evidence for the previously asserted solver comparison. It also qualifies the novelty claim and clarifies reproducibility details. These are useful incremental gains. Final-frame ablation results are removed, and stronger trajectory and regularization explanations lack targeted validation, limiting the overall improvement.
